evidence: Version 2 (image 6) delivers the 'Washed Linen Morning Column' more coherently: the hanging linen drape falls in calm vertical folds that sweep into a continuous linen ground with a believable baseline behind the bottle, and the morning window light reads as soft diffuse frontal glow with faint weave grain, matching the original packshot's high-key illumination. The fluted glass, silver cap and nude grosgrain bow stay fully recognizable, the bow keeps wide horizontal breathing room, and the bottle sits slightly right of center with a soft contact shadow settling into the cloth. The left half stays quiet and carries the serif text column (tracked brand line above a larger tailor's-tag title) at shoulder height, honoring the beside layout and two-column editorial grid. Version 1 (image 5) is weaker: its drape is crumpled with diagonal creases that fight the column concept, the drape-to-ground seam cuts awkwardly close behind the bottle base, the ground texture is noisier, and its text column sits higher and floats away from the shoulder line, making the grid feel accidental rather than set.
remaining_problems: The promised linen-colored vertical stitch rule between the text column and the product column is not visible in either version, so the dual-column grid reads implied rather than drawn.
The text column repeats the brand name 'Chloé' twice instead of brand plus a distinct campaign title, weakening hierarchy.
Contact shadow under the bottle is very faint in version 2; the base could sink slightly deeper into the weave for stronger physical contact.
Ground horizon line behind the bottle is still a fairly straight seam; creases should dissolve more gradually into the cloth plane per the brief.
